answer: When an agent first joins the PoA network it whispers a cryptographic proof of resource burn, like a small saffron‑colored token, to a nearby bridge node that records the stake in a public ledger. The bridge aggregates these proofs and applies quadratic weighting, so that k identities each contributing one unit count only as √k of a single established identity, dramatically raising the cost of spawning many fake nodes. An attacker must therefore expend resources proportional to the square of the desired Sybil count, turning a cheap flood into an economically prohibitive attack.
